title: Mechanistic interpretability: which layer knows what
notes: Positions: fixed-seed (seed 2026) random subset of nn_data/solver_300k.npz, n=50000 split 70/10/20 into train/val/test (35000/5000/10000). All probe scores are on the test split; ablation/census/patching use the test split.
Row convention: row 0 = TOP row of the board (as in nn/encode.py and the website grid). 'Odd/even rows' are counted 1..6 from the BOTTOM (zugzwang convention).
Input planes: me, opponent, ones, first-player-to-move flag; everything is from the side-to-move's perspective.
Forward pass re-implemented in torch from the exported .npz (BatchNorm folded); max |diff| vs nn/numpy_net.py is in checks.

Probes: linear (logistic / softmax / least-squares) on standardised features, full-batch L-BFGS from zero init, L2 1e-4 (1e-3 for the small opp_reply subset), 10 rounds x 10 iterations; each head keeps the test score of its best validation epoch. flat = all C*6*7 activations; pooled = per-channel spatial mean; shuffled = same probe on flat features with permuted train+val labels (test labels real).

Metrics: auc = ROC AUC averaged over columns (binary concepts are single-column), acc = accuracy (multicat: mean over columns), r2 = R^2 averaged over outputs. 'majority' = best constant predictor (auc 0.5).

Normalised skill = (score - chance)/(1 - chance). first_layer = first layer (order input, stem, blocks, pol_conv, val_conv, val_hidden) reaching 90% of the best normalised skill; survives_pooling = best pooled skill >= 80% of best flat skill.

opp_reply: the net's argmax move is played and the successor solved with Pons' solver; label = the opponent's optimal set. Requested opp-n=4000 per model (70/10/20 from the same splits); positions where the net's move ends the game are dropped (see checks.<model>.opp_reply).

opp_net_move: the same net's argmax on the colour-flipped input (planes 0/1 swapped, plane 3 toggled) - an off-distribution input. opp_win_now doubles as opp-move concept (c): the opponent's immediate-win columns = must-block columns.
Threat square = empty cell that would complete four for that side (playable or not). Double threat = 2+ playable immediate wins, or a playable threat with a second threat directly above it.

Channel labels (stem and block outputs, test split): dead if active (>0) on <1% of (position,cell) samples; candidates own-/opponent-threat if Pearson r with that side's threat or immediate-win cells, computed over EMPTY cells only, >= 0.3 and exceeds the other side's; occupancy copy if |r| with mine/theirs/empty cells >= 0.5; column (row/height) detector if the mean 6x7 map holds >= 25% of total activation variance and column (row) main effects hold >= 60% of the map's variance; phase: early/late if |r| of the spatially pooled activation with ply >= 0.6 (note: ply = stone count, so this also catches channels that simply grow with the number of stones). Priority when several apply: threat > occupancy > column > row > phase; otherwise 'mixed'.
Channel content means: [empty playable, empty not playable, mine, theirs]. phase = mean pooled activation [early, mid, late]; phase_idx = (late-early)/(|late|+|early|).

Ablation metrics: agree = argmax (legal) in solver-optimal set; value_acc = argmax WDL == solver outcome; kl = KL(intact || ablated) policy over legal columns; dv = mean |change in P(win)-P(loss)|; missed_win over positions with an own immediate win; missed_block over positions with no own win and exactly one opponent win column. Reported as ablated minus intact.
Block modes: identity (block skipped), zero_branch (residual branch zeroed: identical to identity because block inputs are post-ReLU), mean_branch (branch replaced by its mean over the test split).

Group ablation: channels of one census label in one layer set to 0 (zero) or their per-cell test-split mean (mean); null = 30 random equal-size sets of live channels from the same layer (excluding the group when possible). pct = fraction of null draws below the effect.
Single-channel ablation uses mean ablation; per-channel arrays in interp_channels.json.

Patching: probe direction for opp_win_now column j (logistic weights, raw-activation units, normalised) at the stream layer where that probe is best; step = gap between positive/negative class means along it; 'add' on quiet positions (no immediate win for either side, column j legal), 'subtract' on positions where j is the unique must-block column; d_logit_rel = change in logit j minus mean change of other logits; 20 random unit directions with the same step.
CKA: linear CKA on 5000 test positions between every layer of sup_6x64 and every layer of each other model.
params = parameters of the exported .npz (BatchNorm folded into convolutions).
Runtime: 4330 s total.
phase and ply are linear in the input (ply = stone count), so the phase probe is a sanity check, not a discovery; 'parts used in the early game' is answered by the phase-split ablations.

Opponent double threat

Opponent threat squares on odd rows
Opponent threat squares on even rows
Solver-optimal column set (multi-label)
The net's own argmax move
Solver outcome W/D/L
Solver score of the position

findings.title: Which blocks matter (sup_6x64)
findings.claim: Mean-ablating the residual branch of block1 costs the most solver agreement overall (-0.502); early-game (ply<12) most affected by block1 (-0.476), late-game (ply>=24) by block1 (-0.447).
findings.evidence: identity knock-out agreement deltas: block1 -0.456, block2 -0.254, block3 -0.152, block4 -0.070, block5 -0.046, block6 -0.059
findings.caveat: zero_branch equals identity exactly (block inputs are post-ReLU, so ReLU(h+0)=h); deltas are on 10000 held-out positions.

findings.title: Concepts that need no computation
findings.claim: sup_6x64: heights (r2 0.997), landing_row (acc 1.000), ply (r2 1.000), first_to_move (auc 1.000), phase (acc 0.994) are already decodable from the raw input planes by a linear probe (input score >= 98% of perfect normalised skill), so their layer profile only shows how long the network keeps them, not where it computes them.
findings.evidence: heights at stem/block6: 1.00, 0.99, 0.92; landing_row at stem/block6: 1.00, 1.00, 0.98; ply at stem/block6: 1.00, 1.00, 0.97; first_to_move at stem/block6: 1.00, 1.00, 1.00; phase at stem/block6: 0.95, 0.96, 0.90
findings.caveat: Pooled (position-independent) versions of heights / landing_row are much weaker; see probe_summary.pooled_best.

findings.title: Own move vs opponent's move
findings.claim: sup_6x64: its own move is linearly decodable (net_move acc 0.947 at pol_conv vs 0.331 on raw input); the solver's best opponent reply after that move is weak (opp_reply AUC 0.723 at block6 vs 0.691 on raw input, 0.520 shuffled max); the net's own choice on the colour-flipped board reaches acc 0.731 at block6 (input 0.376).

findings.caveat: opp_reply uses ~3k solved positions per model (see checks), so its probe is data-limited; for az/2x32/ppo no layer beats the raw input on it.
